subject: Final audit: system access sweep & customer data non-exposure confirmation
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Derek Mills <derek.mills@paragonbank.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Final audit: system access sweep & customer data non-exposure confirmation

Derek / Paragon security team,

We completed the full access sweep and forensic hash reconciliation for the June 9th incident window. Summary items attached: access-sweep-summary.csv (sampled event rows), hashes-commit-20270615.txt (SHA256 commit of sampled files), and the audit report on Drive. High-level results: 
- No authenticated accesses to Paragon customer records were observed outside routine processing buckets.
- KV cache snapshots taken during the window were ephemeral and removed; sample hashes match expected ephemeral snapshots (see attached).
- No large data egress patterns detected (no multi-GB downloads from customer-specific indices).

What we did: 24-hour rolling log replay against auth events, KV cache sweep verification, S3 object access pattern analysis, and signature-based detection for exfil tools. Chain-of-custody artifacts and hash lists are attached for your team to validate.

Next steps: please review attachments and confirm if you require additional evidence (full raw logs, longer retention of artifacts for your audit team, or an ATO checklist). We will hold the evidence for 30 days unless you ask us to extend.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: access-sweep-summary.csv (CSV, 2.1MB), hashes-commit-20270615.txt (TXT, signed SHA256), audit-report.pdf (link)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final audit: system access sweep & customer data non-exposure confirmation

Aisha,

Thanks for the package — quick operational notes for the record:
- All sampled logs and hashes were stored in the incident bucket with restricted ACLs; I pushed the signed hash file to our KMS-protected artifacts (hashes-commit-20270615.txt).
- Chain-of-custody email and task IDs: SUP-9872 (audit collection), SUP-9873 (hashing), SUP-9874 (artifact upload).
- I validated there are no retained copies in the analytics staging area; I ran a targeted grep for Paragon tenant IDs (pgn-*) across last-90-day temp objects.

If Paragon wants raw request-level logs we can produce them in a redacted form.

-ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Incident Responder, Redwood Inference

From: Derek Mills <derek.mills@paragonbank.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: security@paragonbank.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final audit: system access sweep & customer data non-exposure confirmation

Aisha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A couple of clarifying questions from our internal review: 
1) Can you confirm whether any model embedding caches associated with Paragon identifiers were persisted beyond 2 hours? We want to be sure ephemeral caches were cleared.
2) The summary mentions no large downloads — did you flag any anomalous small-volume but repeated pulls against a customer index?

If you can mark which files in the CSV correspond to the model-cache sweep vs. auth events that will help our compliance review.

—Derek
Derek Mills
Head of Security, Paragon Bank

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Derek Mills <derek.mills@paragonbank.com>
Cc: aisha.rahman@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final audit: system access sweep & customer data non-exposure confirmation

Derek —

Short answers: 
- Embedding caches: cleared. We enforce a strict ephemeral policy for embedding caches tied to tenant sessions; for Paragon we verified TTL=1h for the window, and a background sweep removed residual shards. Cache-sweep-log.txt (attached) contains timeline entries: create -> evict -> confirmation hash. Sample entry below:

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Derek / Paragon security team,
> 
> We completed the full access sweep and forensic hash reconciliation for the June 9th incident window. Summary items attached: access-sweep-summary.csv (sampled event rows), hashes-commit-20270615.txt (SHA256 commit of sampled files), and the audit report on Drive. High-level results: 
> - No authenticated accesses to Paragon customer records were observed outside routine processing buckets.
> - KV cache snapshots taken during the window were ephemeral and removed; sample hashes match expected ephemeral snapshots (see attached).
> - No large data egress patterns detected (no multi-GB downloads from customer-specific indices).
> 
> What we did: 24-hour rolling log replay against auth events, KV cache sweep verification, S3 object access pattern analysis, and signature-based detection for exfil tools. Chain-of-custody artifacts and hash lists are attached for your team to validate.

Additional detail: we observed a handful of low-volume repeated reads (sub-100KB per request) from an internal monitoring task that erroneously targeted a test index with Paragon tagging. Those reads were from our monitoring agent and stopped once we updated the target list at 02:14 UTC; there is no evidence of downstream aggregation or download. Rows flagged in access-sweep-summary.csv with tag "monitoring-read" indicate those events.

Let us know if Paragon would like the raw (redacted) request IDs for those reads.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: cache-sweep-log.txt (TXT, 18KB)

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Derek Mills <derek.mills@paragonbank.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Final audit: system access sweep & customer data non-exposure confirmation

Derek / Paragon security team —

Closing the loop from our side. To summarize:
- No evidence of customer data exposure or exfiltration related to the June 9th window.
- Embedding caches were ephemeral and successfully swept; cache-sweep-log.txt attached.
- Small repeated reads were internal monitoring activity and not an exfil pattern; we included the flagged rows in access-sweep-summary.csv.

We will retain the signed artifact bundle (hashes-commit-20270615.txt) and the raw, redacted request logs for 30 days in the incident bucket. If you need extended retention or want us to deliver a sealed copy for your records, reply and we'll coordinate a secure transfer (SCP or SFTP with mutual auth).

Please reply-all with a short acknowledgement when you are satisfied with closure, or list any outstanding evidence you need.

Best,
Aisha
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Related ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/tickets/PRD-48219
Attachments: access-sweep-summary.csv, hashes-commit-20270615.txt, cache-sweep-log.txt
